page0.text:
And so the day passes until lunchtime.
We meet up on the roof per unspoken agreement, and I tell Tohsaka what happened last night.
As a result...

page1.text:
"So, what!?
You're saying that Zouken Matou is Assassin's Master, and he tried to kill you, not Saber!?"
Tohsaka suddenly gets angry at me.

page2.text:
"Y-yeah, what's your problem?"
"I'm not the one with a problem!
The way you told it, Zouken tried to kill you after he beat Saber! That doesn't make sense. It sounds completely backwards!"

page3.text:
Tohsaka leans in and glares at me, irritated.
We're behind the water tower, which has become our usual meeting spot. I unconsciously back up just a few centimeters, intimidated by her spirit that feels closer to hostility.

page4.text:
"Hey. Are you listening to me? Doesn't your story sound wrong to you?"
Tohsaka shoots me a glare full of irritation and loathing.

page5.text:
"Oof."
Her attitude is overwhelming enough, but her being this close is making me very uneasy.
I don't have any more room to back up in this tight space.
I'm like a rat—I mean, human trapped in a bag.

page6.text:
"Um...what's wrong with what I said?"
"The priority is all wrong. You were alone with Zouken, but he didn't try to kill you.
While it's great for him that Assassin won, as long as there was a chance he would lose, Zouken should have targeted Saber's Master first."

page7.text:
"...That makes sense, but are you saying that
Zouken was confident that Assassin would beat Saber?"

page8.text:
"No way. Even you know that Assassin is weaker than Saber, right? Zouken wouldn't take a risk like that.
...So he must have had some other reason.
I can think of two."
